item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Basic settings guide; how-to content Steven doesn't engage with.] Grand Theft Auto 6 features some key settings for those who feel the open-world game moves too slowly.
item.content:encoded: Now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, players are discovering that Rockstar Games' latest feels more like Red Dead Redemption 2 than GTA 5. Rockstar Games builds on the work it did in its open-world western and applies it to the context of a modern city. That’s a big part of why it's so successful, but that might make some players nervous. While GTA 6 moves at a quicker pace, movement can still feel a little slower than you might expect.

item.title: How Long Does It Take To Beat GTA 6?
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] GTA 6 has the biggest story in the series' history. Here's how long it will take you to beat it.
item.content:encoded: If you couldn't guess by its 210 GB file size, Grand Theft Auto 6 is gigantic. Rockstar's latest open-world game is stuffed to the brim with things to do and steal. It also sports the beefiest story of any GTA game to date. Jason and Lucia star in a sprawling crime epic that takes the couple all around the state of Leonida. While it's difficult to put a consistent hour count on a true 100% playthrough of GTA 6, we do know that you won't be able to binge it all in one long weekend.

item.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Miss Wormwood Quote Is Still Among the Smartest in Comic Strip History
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not a game.] Looking back at Miss Wormwood's best moments in Calvin and Hobbes
item.content:encoded: Bill Watterson walked a few different tightropes when he created Calvin and Hobbes, one of which involved Calvin's relationship with school. It would've been easy to make it simply antagonistic, with Calvin as the hero fighting back against the dark forces of educational conformity, a bit like a comic adaptation of Pink Floyd's "Another Brick in the Wall." Any number of later webcomics that were unsubtly inspired by Calvin and Hobbes went this way, at least at first.

item.title: 8 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics Starring Cowboys
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not gaming/core content.] Gary Larson’s comic strip The Far Side loved to parody cowboys in the Old West. Here are the eight best
item.content:encoded: Gary Larson, the comedy genius behind The Far Sidecomic strip, loved to turn things into their opposites. Serious, brilliant scientists were cast as childish dummies who drop everything when they hear an ice cream truck pass by. Simple-minded cows could be so smart that they plot the deaths of their owners. As for cowboys, the manly men of the Old West, Larson loved to portray them as meek and cowardly.

item.title: 10 Sci-Fi Books You Need to Read Before At Least Once In Your Life
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, not video game or prestige film/TV coverage.] The ultimate reading list for mind-bending, genre-defining speculative fiction
item.content:encoded: Science fiction remains one of storytelling's most expansive playgrounds, capable of charting distant space just as easily as it exposes the imminent horrors of near-future technology. At its peak, sci-fi uses invented technology and distant planets to interrogate what it means to be human, cracking open eternal philosophical questions that more grounded genres simply can’t.

item.title: 66 Years Later, William Shatner's Forgotten 'Twilight Zone' Is Still a Haunting Masterpiece
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; old episode isn't new prestige/anticipated project.] The Twilight Zone episode “Nick of Time” is top-tier Shatner
item.content:encoded: “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet” is one of the all-time great episodes of The Twilight Zone. Starring William Shatner, the story is about a man who is taking his first flight after having had a nervous breakdown. During the flight, he looks out the window and sees a creature, called a gremlin, on the wing that taunts him and tears apart pieces of the plane. No one can see the gremlin but him, and even his own wife attributes it to his fragile mental state. The story is a brilliant commentary on paranoia and Shatner was captivating in the role. It was so good that it sometimes overshadows Shatner’s other great episode of The Twilight Zone, which premiered 66 years ago today.

item.title: 63 Years Later, the Best 'Peanuts' Sally Line Is Still an Iconic Comic Strip Quote
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about decades-old comic strip.] In Peanuts, it's Sally Brown vs. school
item.content:encoded: Charlie Brown might be the unluckiest character in the Western canon. The degree to which the universe conspires to dump misfortune directly on his head over and over is the beating heart of Charles Schulz's Peanuts. If you've got any problems at all, you can check in on good ol' Charlie Brown and be slightly cheered up by the knowledge that at least you've got it better than him.

item.title: 30 Years Later, One of the Greatest ‘X-Files’ Episodes is Still a Misunderstood Masterpiece
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show, not horror.] “Musings of a Cigarette Smoking Man” is a classic X-Files epsiode that many fans misunderstand
item.content:encoded: For the first three seasons of The X-Files, the writers kept you guessing, not only with regard to the show’s greater mysteries about aliens, but also about its most intriguing character. The Cigarette Smoking Man, played by William B. Davis, begins the series as a shadowy, silent character in the first episode. He looks on as Agent Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson) is given her not-too-subtle orders to undermine Agent Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and his work on the X-Files. He goes on to appear sparingly, just a few times each season, to stop Mulder and Scully from getting too close to the secrets he’s spent decades covering up.

Among the story's many memorable encounters is Circe, a powerful sorceress who turns Odysseus' men into pigs. Played by Samantha Morton, Circe is responsible for one of the film's most unsettling sequences, which involves a human head being transformed into that of a pig.

item.title: Robert Pattinson's Batman Movie Franchise Is Officially Finished
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise churn (DC/Batman), fans being robbed of trilogy gossip.] With Pattinson being cast as Bond, DC fans are once again being robbed of a good Batman trilogy
item.content:encoded: With Robert Pattinson confirmed to be the next James Bond, one of the biggest takeaways is that Matt Reeves’ The Batman series will likely end with The Batman: Part II. Pattinson is signed on for three films as Bond, and while that’s one less film than the four-film deal that Amazon MGM Studios was seeking for the other Bond contenders, it’s pretty hard to imagine that Pattinson will juggle the role of 007 with an ongoing commitment to DC — much less Battinson’s integration into the wider DCU, which some DC fans had hoped for. To be clear, nothing has been confirmed about the status of a third The Batman movie, but the latest news combined with the extreme delays facing The BatmanPartII feel like a pretty clear indication that the Batmobile has hit a dead end and will need yet another reboot.

Following the closure of Mass Effect developer BioWare and the cancellation of the next game in the series, excitement for Fate of the Old Republic has somehow grown even larger. But we haven't heard much about the spiritual successor to Knights of the Old Republic, which Hudson also directed, since it was revealed back in 2025. In an interview with Empire, Kevin Feige said that Secret Wars “is a whole other genre of story” compared to the upcoming Avengers:Doomsday. While that comment will be more useful once Doomsday releases on Dec. 18, Feige seems to be hinting that the movie won’t be quite as grim as Doomsday, which is expected to bea multiversal bloodbath.

item.content:encoded: The story in Númenor has involved a lot of family drama. Captain Elendil (Lloyd Owen) is one of the leaders of the Faithful, a Númenórean group who believes in preserving the kingdom’s connection to the Elves and the Valar. His daughter Eärien (Ema Horvath) allied herself with Pharazôn and his son, Kemen (Leon Wadham), encouraging her father to renounce his faith and pledge loyalty to the new king. She participated in the arrest of the Faithful’s leaders, though she helped her father escape.

item.title: Netflix's New 12-Part Sci-Fi Mystery Already Feels Like a Masterpiece Just 3 Episodes In
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Generic streaming sci-fi review, not prestige or horror content.] Fool Night turns a bleak sci-fi premise into an visually stunning mystery that rewards patience.
item.content:encoded: From a surprise collaboration between two iconic anime studios, Sunrise and Shaft, Fool Night imagines a future world where the sun has long disappeared, leaving humanity with the unusual solution of turning volunteer humans into plants for oxygen. It's a bleak setup, made all the more gripping by a visual identity that constantly juxtaposes human decay with budding flora. Netflix only provided us with the first three episodes (out of 12 total) for review, and I'm entirely hooked. Between its sharp character work, unsettling world-building, and melancholic atmosphere, Fool Night is shaping up to be one of the most striking new shows of Fall.

item.title: 7 Best Things About the Original Xbox That Aren't Halo, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old Xbox; not a new announcement.] We celebrate the original Xbox for introducing Halo, but the hardware and its software library offered plenty of other attractions worth remembering.
item.content:encoded: When Microsoft entered the console market with its Xbox brand, people outside the company didn’t necessarily have high hopes. Throughout the 1990s, the industry was dominated by Japanese hardware companies like Nintendo, Sega, and Sony. But Microsoft meant business, and its first console effort provided some excellent reasons to give the brand a chance.

item.title: 15 Years Later, Jamie Lannister’s Best Game of Thrones Quote Is an All-Time Fantasy Hit
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; 15-year-old quote analysis, not new.] 'Game of Thrones' has plenty of iconic quotes. But Jamie Lannister's best sums up his downfall.
item.content:encoded: Many factors have helped make George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire one of the most beloved fantasy series of all time, and one big reason is HBO’s adaptation of the dark fantasy epic by showrunners David Benioff and D. B. Weiss. The eight-season adaptation brought Martin’s vast, stunning world and complex central characters to life. Jaime Lannister, played by Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, was one such character. And like many others in Game of Thrones, he had poetic one-liners that captured his nature and helped define his place in the story over the years.

item.title: 7 Decades Later, the Most Satisfying Movie of All Time Is Free on YouTube
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Sidney Lumet’s 12 Angry Men is one of the best, simplest films ever made and its free to stream on YouTube
item.content:encoded: 12 Angry Men begins at the very end of a trial, just as the jury is about to go deliberate. This is a murder case where a son is being accused of stabbing his father to death. The judge reminds the jury of their duty, and that the sentence for this person, if convicted, will be death. Silently, the young man who barely looks to be out of high school looks at the jury and a couple of members look back. Then the jury goes off into the jury room.
